title: Stash & Splay latency vs cost sweep (draft)
body:
Summary:
This is a working sweep comparing two KV-prefetch approaches we prototyped: "stash" (aggressive eager prefetch of likely prefixes) and "splay" (adaptive selective prefetch guided by recent-turn intent signal). Purpose is to capture tradeoffs across short-session microbursts, steady conversational traffic, and sustained long-generation workloads.

Quick takeaway (working):
- Stash reduces p90/p99 for fast microbursts by raising short-term cache hit rate, lowering tail in burst windows.
- Splay is generally more cost-stable for sustained workloads and reduces cache pollution under long-lived sessions.
- There is no single winner; pick policy by workload class or dynamically switch based on detected burstiness.

Methodology:
- Platform: Redwood internal cluster (x4 A100-like nodes) using runtime v0.87-proto with identical batching knobs.
- Instruments: client-side traced latency, server-side token accounting, cost model = GPU-time * instance rate + minor infra overhead approximated from infra-metering.
- Each experiment: 30 minute run, 10 warmup minutes discarded, 3 runs per cell, median reported.
- Workload shapes: microburst (10k sessions concentrated in 60s window), conversational (steady 2k qps, avg 60 tokens/session), sustained long (continuous 500 qps, avg 250 tokens).

Workload table (median of runs) — ASCII results:

| Workload   | Policy | KV hit % | p50 (ms) | p90 (ms) | p99 (ms) | qps  | $ / 10k sessions | Notes |
|------------|--------|----------|----------|----------|----------|------|------------------|-------|
| Microburst | Stash  | 68       | 35       | 120      | 420      | 180  | $12.40           | best p90/p99 on burst window |
| Microburst | Splay  | 54       | 28       | 150      | 610      | 160  | $14.70           | lower p50, higher tail, higher cost due to retrying |
| Conversn   | Stash  | 61       | 48       | 160      | 720      | 120  | $22.50           | slightly better hit, slightly better p90 |
| Conversn   | Splay  | 58       | 46       | 175      | 790      | 118  | $23.10           | similar behavior, marginally more stable cost |
| Sustained  | Stash  | 40       | 120      | 380      | 1100     | 60   | $48.30           | cache pollution shows, higher cost |
| Sustained  | Splay  | 42       | 115      | 360      | 1020     | 62   | $47.00           | better for long tails, slightly cheaper per-session |

Notes on numbers: cost model is coarse — includes GPU library overhead, amortized kv-index memory pressure interpreted as slight effective throughput shrink. Absolute dollars are not billing values, they are for relative comparison only.

Observations and interpretation:
- Burst sensitivity: Stash wins when the workload has a high fraction of short context replays (e.g., repeated prompts). By prefetching likely KV segments aggressively we reduce I/O stalls and p90/p99 substantially. The tradeoff is wasted prefetch work during sustained traffic which lowers hit efficiency.
- Pollution and churn: In sustained long workloads, stash brings more pollution (evicting useful long-term entries) and increases backend work, translating to a higher cost-per-session. Splay's selective logic retains high-value entries longer and avoids waste.
- p50 vs tail: Splay sometimes shows slightly better p50 because it avoids locking the prefetch pipeline for low-latency fast queries; stash can add small overhead to p50 in some shapes.
- Cost inflection: There is a non-linear knee: for burstiness > ~30% of sessions falling in <5s hot windows, stash's cost wins thanks to avoided retries and lower external I/O. Below that, splay generally yields better amortized cost.

Representative ascii delta-snapshot (p90 vs $):

p90 (ms)    |   $ per 10k
------------+--------------
Stash: 160  |   $22.5
Splay: 175  |   $23.1
(Conversational)

Policy tuning notes (actionable):
- Heuristic: detect burst windows by short-term increase in session arrivals (5x baseline in 30s) and flip to stash for a short hold window (60-180s).
- TTL adapt: lower aggressive prefetch TTL for stash during sustained periods to reduce pollution.
- Hybrid: start with splay, enable stash when predicted next-turn repeat prob > 0.6 (model hint).

Risks and open questions:
- Measurement noise: p99 is sensitive to infra jitter; need more runs across regions and underlying kernel variants.
- Cost model fidelity: this used an internal approximation; run billing-coupled experiments for customer-facing guidance.
- Interaction with quantization / kernel selection: stash's CPU/GPU scheduling profile could change when models are quantized differently. Need cross-product sweep.

Next steps (short list):
- Run regionally distributed microburst tests (EU/APAC) to validate latency tails under cross-region routing (owner: Diego).
- Integrate precise billing counters into experiments and re-evaluate $/10k for final recommendation (owner: Priya).
- Prototype a simple burst-detector + policy flip in the runtime for end-to-end A/B (owner: eng-runtime team, PR referenced).

Appendix (raw run notes):
- Warmup handled by synthetic filler sessions; observed cold-start noise ~12% of p99 for first 5 minutes if warmup omitted.
- Prefetch window sizing: stash aggressively requested 3 prefix pages ahead; splay requested 1–2 based on recency score.
- Memory footprint: stash runs increased KV index working set by ~18% leading to minor throughput pressure on saturated nodes.

Draft status: experimental sweep. Looking for feedback on extra dimensions to add (multi-model mix, embeddings-heavy traffic, token-score informed prefetch).
